scope: Document.load(recovery: .readOnlyPartial) — the whole-life write refusal and the registry's blind spot
statement: a Document opened via Document.load(recovery: .readOnlyPartial) writes NOTHING across its whole life, including across close(): no op appended, the .md byte-identical, the pending file untouched, no checkpoint, no seal — every mutation entry point (setFullText, setParagraph, insertParagraph, deleteParagraph, reorder, flushBurstNow) consults the writability choke point (rejectMutationIfNotWritable / requireWritable) before it would reach opStore.append or pending.recordChange, held not by the entry points alone but by a CENSUS over every Document*.swift function reaching those two calls, so a mutation added later cannot quietly skip the choke point. Before this rung existed, the refusal above it (M9-OL-002/003) was the floor: an unreadable op-log file or unlistable ops directory REFUSED the whole document, offering the writer nothing but the bare error. EditorHost's recovery action wires the read-only load WITHOUT a second call to documentStore.register — the census over EditorHost.swift holds the register call count at exactly one (the normal path's), so a partial-view Document stays outside the registry MCP's read_document/add_note resolve through and is reachable only from the pane that opened it — born with the milestone (spec §4)
reachability: LIVE — any refusal rung the ladder's Open Read-Only action offers

scope: RecoveryCause.classify + RecoveryPaneModel + RecoveryBannerModel — the refusal names its cause; the return is offered where a view is open and auto-opened from the refusal pane
statement: a document-load refusal is classified into one of three named causes before the pane renders anything (RecoveryCause.classify, reading only the REFUSAL error, never partial content): a dataless iCloud stub (icloudNotDownloaded) triggers a download, waits, and auto-opens editable the moment the file reads — and NEVER offers the read-only rung; an unreadable-for-another-reason file (unreadableFile) offers both the read-only view and Restore, with the reason riding in the pane's detail; an unlistable ops directory (unlistableOpsDirectory) offers Restore only, because nothing is enumerable to read partially. The return is asymmetric by where the writer is: from the refusal pane the fix auto-opens editable (RecoveryPaneModel's poller fires onOpenEditable once isReadable turns true, for both the stub and the fixed-permissions cases); from an already-open read-only view the fix is OFFERED, never yanked — RecoveryBannerModel.offersReopen only turns true once every named file reads again, and the model exposes no reload callback of its own to misuse. Before this ladder existed, every refusal rendered the same bare error message regardless of cause, offering no wait, no read, and no differentiated return — born with the milestone (spec §3)
reachability: LIVE — every document-load refusal the ladder classifies

statement: the writer's own press — never anything automatic (spec §6's 'no auto-quarantine, ever') — moves an unreadable op-log file byte-identically (one NSFileCoordinator, coordinating source-for-moving and destination) into .maugham/conflicts/quarantined-ops/ and writes a QuarantineRecord (docId, originalName, quarantinedAt, the read error at the time, status .held) beside it; a dataless iCloud stub is refused (QuarantineError.datalessStub) rather than moved, so the verb never fights the wait-and-retry rung's own download; two quarantines of the same original name in the same stamp millisecond both survive via a disambiguating suffix rather than one overwriting the other. The document then opens fully editable through the one retryFullLoad path. Reached from BOTH surfaces the spec names: the refusal pane's Set the File Aside and Keep Writing action (offered only for RecoveryCause.unreadableFile — RecoveryPaneModel.offersSetAside is false for the iCloud-stub and unlistable-directory causes, which name no single readable-but-broken file to move) and the read-only banner's typing-refusal offer (RecoveryBannerModel.setAsideOffered, raised by noteTypingRefused and lowered the instant every named file reads again); both call the SAME verb (quarantineAndContinue()), one guarded against a stale selection (the pane's three minted actions) and one deliberately unguarded (the banner's, built fresh per render from the doc the body is rendering). The offer is said in the writer's words at every site — 'Set the File Aside and Keep Writing', 'kept safe … merged back when it returns' — and never says 'quarantine' at the writer

scope: OpLogQuarantine.attemptReturn + RecoveredHistory.report — the return merge and the orphan report
statement: attemptReturn requires a clean, fully VERIFIED read of the quarantined bytes before anything moves: a still-unreadable file or one whose lines fail to decode (a torn tail) leaves the record .held rather than merging a partial view (spec §5 step 1 — salvage is the integrity path's job, not a merge input). A clean read merges by the existing cross-device sync rules (ADR 0012, opId-ordered, last-writer-wins-per-paragraph) and NEVER overwrites an existing destination file: if sync already delivered the same device's file back while it was set aside, the archive stays exactly where it is and the record is marked .superseded rather than moved a second time onto something already there. A sidecar rewrite that fails AFTER a successful move-back self-heals at READ time — records(forDocId:in:) reconciles a stale .held record whose quarantined bytes are gone against an already-returned destination file — rather than stranding the writer on a 'still set aside' notice forever. RecoveredHistory.report is the pure accounting behind the honest half: for every paragraph in the RETURNED file's own derivation, it is EITHER in the merged draft's sequence OR in the orphan report, proven by a 200-trial randomized property test over interleaved two-device op sets with sequence keyframes — never lost, never counted in both. Reached opportunistically — EditorHost's auto-return sweep on every normal document open, guarded off a read-only recovery bind — and explicitly, the History pane's Retry; the report reaches the writer through HistoryPane's standing notice ('N paragraphs … aren't in your draft — View', or 'Recovered history merged — nothing was missing' for zero orphans) and RecoveredHistorySheet, whose Append to End lands each orphan as an ordinary new insertParagraph op against the OPEN document only — rewindable, undoable, overwriting nothing — disabled with the honest reason 'Open the document to append' when the document is closed
